This article describes new features in .NET 11. It was last updated for Preview 5.

.NET 11 is currently in preview. The final release is expected in November 2026. You can [download .NET 11 here](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

## .NET runtime

The .NET 11 runtime includes:

*   Updated minimum hardware requirements for x86/x64 and Arm64 architectures, requiring more modern instruction sets to improve performance and reduce maintenance complexity.
*   Runtime-native async (Runtime Async), which produces cleaner stack traces and lower overhead. Runtime Async no longer requires `<EnablePreviewFeatures>true</EnablePreviewFeatures>` for projects that target `net11.0`. The runtime libraries themselves are compiled with `runtime-async=on`.
*   JIT improvements for bounds check elimination, redundant checked context removal, switch expression folding, constant-folding `SequenceEqual`, and redundant branch elimination. There are also new Arm SVE2 intrinsics and improved hardware-intrinsic cost modeling.

For more information, see [What's new in the .NET 11 runtime](runtime).

## .NET libraries

The .NET 11 libraries include new APIs for:

*   [Process](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.process) expansion with run-and-capture helpers, fire-and-forget launches, `SafeProcessHandle` lifecycle methods, and tighter handle control.
*   Compression, including improved Base64 APIs, new methods for ZIP archive entries, Zstandard compression in [System.IO.Compression](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.compression), and CRC32 validation when reading ZIP entries.
*   System.Text.Json improvements, including generic type info retrieval, [JsonNamingPolicy.PascalCase](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.json.jsonnamingpolicy.pascalcase#system-text-json-jsonnamingpolicy-pascalcase), per-member naming policy overrides, type-level ignore conditions, F# discriminated union support, [Utf8JsonWriter.Reset](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.json.utf8jsonwriter.reset) with options, and `SerializeAsyncEnumerable` overloads for `PipeWriter` targets and top-level values (NDJSON) output.
*   Built-in OpenTelemetry metrics for [MemoryCache](/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.extensions.caching.memory.memorycache).
*   Discriminated-union scaffolding (`UnionAttribute` and `IUnion`) in [System.Runtime.CompilerServices](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.compilerservices).
*   Tar archive format selection and GNU sparse format 1.0 support.
*   `Console` support for the `FORCE_COLOR` environment variable.
*   TLS handshake hardening and certificate-validation alerts on Linux.
*   HTTP/2 automatic downgrade for Windows authentication.
*   LINQ join improvements, including `FullJoin` and tuple-returning `Join` and `GroupJoin` overloads, across [Enumerable](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.linq.enumerable), [Queryable](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.linq.queryable), and [AsyncEnumerable](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.linq.asyncenumerable).
*   A new [X25519DiffieHellman](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x25519diffiehellman) class for X25519 key exchange.
*   Generic overloads on [Random](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.random) — `NextInteger<T>` and `NextBinaryFloat<T>` — that work with any numeric generic type.
*   [EqualityComparer<T>.Create](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.equalitycomparer-1.create) factory method that creates a comparer from a key selector.
*   [QuicStream.Priority](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.quic.quicstream.priority#system-net-quic-quicstream-priority) for HTTP/3 stream prioritization.
*   Video MIME type constants in [MediaTypeNames.Video](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.mime.mediatypenames.video).

For more information, see [What's new in the .NET 11 libraries](libraries).

## .NET SDK

The .NET 11 SDK includes:

*   Smaller SDK installers on Linux and macOS through assembly deduplication, with additional savings by skipping crossgen for `DotnetTools`\-only assemblies.
*   Improved [CA1873](../../../fundamentals/code-analysis/quality-rules/ca1873) code analyzer with reduced noise and clearer diagnostic messages.
*   Support for creating and editing solution filters (`.slnf`) from the `dotnet sln` CLI.
*   File-based app support for `#:include` to split apps across multiple files.
*   A new `dotnet run -e` option to pass environment variables from the command line.
*   `dotnet watch` improvements, including Aspire app-host integration, automatic crash recovery, and device selection for MAUI and mobile projects.
*   OpenTelemetry replaces Application Insights for CLI telemetry.
*   Foundation for a NativeAOT entry point for the `dotnet` CLI.

For more information, see [What's new in the SDK for .NET 11](sdk).

## ASP.NET Core

## C# 15

*   [Collection expression arguments](../../../csharp/whats-new/csharp-15#collection-expression-arguments)

For information about new C# features, see [What's new in C# 15](../../../csharp/whats-new/csharp-15).

### TLS handshake hardening

Two [System.Net.Security](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.security) items improve TLS (Transport Layer Security) reliability:

*   [SslStream](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.security.sslstream) server-side handshake bounds-checking fixes in `TlsFrameHelper` close several edge cases that could surface as `IOException` on malformed ClientHello records.

[HttpClient](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.http.httpclient) automatically downgrades to HTTP/1.1 when a request requires Windows authentication (NTLM/Negotiate) over HTTP/2. *   `MediaTypeNames.Video.Mpeg` — `"video/mpeg"`
*   `MediaTypeNames.Video.Ogg` — `"video/ogg"`
*   `MediaTypeNames.Video.QuickTime` — `"video/quicktime"`
*   `MediaTypeNames.Video.WebM` — `"video/webm"`

These join the existing `MediaTypeNames.Application`, `MediaTypeNames.Image`, `MediaTypeNames.Text`, and `MediaTypeNames.Multipart` classes.

## Unsafe API accessibility

.NET 11 removes the `[RequiresUnsafe]` attribute from a large set of APIs that take pointer parameters. Previously, calling these methods from code that used `unsafe` blocks still required a project-level `<AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks>` setting because the attribute enforced that requirement independently. Now, only the standard `unsafe` block or method modifier is required.

Affected APIs include:

*   [Buffer.MemoryCopy](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.buffer.memorycopy)
*   [ReadOnlySpan<T>.ReadOnlySpan<T>(Void\*, Int32)](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.readonlyspan-1.-ctor#system-readonlyspan-1-ctor\(system-void*-system-int32\)) and [Span<T>.Span<T>(Void\*, Int32)](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.span-1.-ctor#system-span-1-ctor\(system-void*-system-int32\))
*   [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.compilerservices.unsafe) pointer methods such as `AsRef`, `Read`, `Write`, and `Copy`
*   [System.Runtime.InteropServices.NativeMemory](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.interopservices.nativememory) methods
*   [System.Text.Encoding](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding) pointer overloads (all encoding classes)
*   [System.Numerics.Vector](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.numerics.vector) pointer-based `Load` and `Store` methods
*   Interop marshalling types in [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshalling](/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.interopservices.marshalling)

This change reduces friction for advanced scenarios such as interop authoring, memory-mapped files, and low-level buffer manipulation, where unsafe context is already required by the calling code.

## Breaking Changes Affecting Your App in .NET 11

### 1. GZipStream empty-output check ⚠️ **BROKEN**

### 2. TAR archives with invalid checksums ⚠️ **BROKEN**
**Your code:** Reads hand-crafted TARs that may have bad checksums.  
**Change:** `TarReader` now validates checksums and throws `InvalidDataException` on mismatch.  
**Fix:** Wrap reads in `try/catch (InvalidDataException)`, or fix the legacy tool to write correct checksums.

### 3. ZipArchive.CreateAsync lazy loading ⚠️ **BROKEN**
**Your code:** Relies on entries being lazily loaded when accessing `.Entries`.  
**Change:** `CreateAsync` now **eagerly** loads the central directory. Exceptions from malformed entries surface at `CreateAsync` time, not when accessing `Entries`. If you deferred work expecting lazy reads, that timing has changed.  
**Fix:** Move error handling to the `await CreateAsync(...)` call. This is actually better for async correctness (no hidden sync I/O).

### 4. MemoryStream large allocations
**No specific .NET 11 breaking change** targets `MemoryStream` capacity. However, note the new **CRC32 validation on ZIP entries** — if your large `MemoryStream` backs a `ZipArchive` for reading, corrupted entries will now throw `InvalidDataException`. The `MemoryStream` itself should work as before.
